Title: Diagnosis of test `testGenerateURLFragment`
Details: The test `testGenerateURLFragment` checks whether HTML entities such as `"` are correctly escaped to their corresponding character by the `StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment` method. However, the test failure indicates that this is not the case. Following the execution path, we find that `StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment` is not escaping any HTML code; instead, it is using its input `toolTipText` as is. Consequently, un-escaped strings are being returned, which leads to the error demonstrated by the test.

The test `['org.apache.commons.csv.CSVRecordTest.testToMapWithNoHeader()']` failed.
The test looks like:

```java
171 :     @Test
172 :     public void testToMapWithNoHeader() throws Exception {
173 :        final CSVParser parser =  CSVParser.parse("a,b", CSVFormat.newFormat(','));
174 :        final CSVRecord shortRec = parser.iterator().next();
175 :        Map<String, String> map = shortRec.toMap(); // error occurred here
178 :     }
```

It failed with the following error message and call stack:

```
java.lang.NullPointerException
	at org.apache.commons.csv.CSVRecord.putIn(CSVRecord.java:180)
	at org.apache.commons.csv.CSVRecord.toMap(CSVRecord.java:214)
	at org.apache.commons.csv.CSVRecordTest.testToMapWithNoHeader(CSVRecordTest.java:175)
```

Start by calling the `get_failing_tests_covered_classes` function.

The test failure occurs due to a NullPointerException happening inside the method CSVRecord.toMap(), specifically at CSVRecord.putIn(). This indicates that there might be a null object being dereferenced in these methods.

Given the test, the input CSV data "a,b" does not have a header defined in the CSVFormat newFormat(','). This means the CSVRecord won't have header names mapped, likely causing a null reference when calling toMap() which attempts to map headers to their values.

Next, I will examine the toMap() method code in the CSVRecord class to understand how it handles no-header cases and why a NullPointerException might arise.
